title: AI and Edge Computing for Scientific Research
description: Scientific discovery is entering a new era shaped by the rapid expansion of autonomous sensing systems and artificial intelligence operating directly at the edge. Platforms such as the Sage Grande Testbed and emerging European edge-computing testbeds are creating unprecedented opportunities to collect, analyze, and act on multimodal environmental and urban data in real time. Yet many foundational questions remain about how to design, integrate, and scale AI@Edge infrastructure to support transformative science across domains, from ecology and climate to agriculture, hazards, and urban systems. This workshop convened forward-looking researchers from the United States and Europe to explore shared challenges and opportunities in developing interoperable AI-enabled distributed instrumentation. Participants represented communities spanning environmental sensing, cyberinfrastructure, and artificial intelligence. The workshop examined how edge AI can accelerate scientific discovery and support the collaborative goals of initiatives such as DISCOVER-US, NAIRR, and EU digital research programs.

title: CV4Ecology 2026: Computer Vision for Ecology Workshop
description: As an instructor at CV4Ecology 2026, I delivered the lecture "What's Next? Rules of Thumb for Improving Results" and provided specialized training in ecological data analysis with artificial intelligence. Over three intensive weeks, participants shared ideas, code, and thoughtful discussions on the challenges of processing diverse types of ecological data. The workshop explored a rich variety of ecological problems and data types, from acoustic monitoring to camera trap imagery and multisensor approaches. Participants collaborated on real-world conservation challenges and built practical skills for implementing AI-driven solutions in biodiversity monitoring.

title: Online Workshop: Machine Learning for Biodiversity Monitoring
description: During this workshop, we presented our latest research on the development of a bird song detector pipeline for the Doñana National Park. We discussed the challenges of working with acoustic data and the strategies we used to overcome them. We also presented the best model we obtained and the confusion matrix results, showing the performance of our model in identifying bird species.

title: Seminario: El papel de la IA en la ecología, cómo transformar imágenes en datos
organizer: Grupo de Ecoinformática de la AEET
description: El seminario pretende explorar la creciente intersección entre la inteligencia artificial (IA) y la ecología, centrándose en cómo la IA puede transformar imágenes en datos para impulsar la investigación y la conservación de la naturaleza. El seminario aborda la definición de IA y su relevancia en el contexto ecológico, destacando casos prácticos que ilustran su aplicación en la recolección y análisis de datos ecológicos. El objetivo principal de la charla es familiarizar a las personas participantes con el potencial y las aplicaciones prácticas de la IA en el campo de la ecología. Se discutirán herramientas y técnicas específicas de IA que ya están disponibles y se exploran errores comunes que suelen cometerse desde la perspectiva de la ecología al utilizar estas tecnologías. Además, se enfatiza la importancia de una colaboración interdisciplinaria entre ecólogos y expertos en IA para abordar los desafíos ambientales de manera efectiva. En resumen, la charla busca inspirar a los participantes a considerar cómo la IA puede mejorar y ampliar su trabajo en la conservación y comprensión de los ecosistemas naturales.
